Quantum information, error correction and photonic computing

From Qubits to Photonic Fault-Tolerant Computing

A seven-level self-study course from phase and measurement through error correction, logical operations, magic states, 2D color codes, measurement-based computing and photonic fusion. It connects codes, circuits, decoders, photon sources and control to the reliability and resource costs of a computation.

Responsible editor: Hyun-Jung Kim · AI assistance: OpenAI Codex · 2026-11-27

7 levels · 28 sections · Korean PDFs

Combined edition

PDF 43 pages

An independently authored self-study monograph, rather than a transcript of a live lecture or Q&A. Korean PDFs are available as a compilation and seven separate levels.

Reading guide

Start with Levels 1–2 to connect quantum states and measurement to noise. Levels 3–5 develop encoding, safe logical operations and the circuit costs of color codes. Levels 6–7 translate these ideas into adaptive measurements and photonic fusion.

Prerequisites: high-school complex numbers and matrix multiplication. The compilation includes a notation guide on page 2. Four self-check questions appear in Levels 1–3: two, one and one respectively. Follow the derivations in the PDFs with your own calculations.

Seven levels

  1. Level 1 PDF 7 pages

    Foundations of Quantum Information

    States, measurements, entanglement and circuits

    Starting with interference, this level shows how relative phase changes measurement probabilities. Bloch vectors, projective measurements, Bell entanglement and teleportation connect gate operations to the quantum information that later levels protect.

    Annotate →PDF ↗Download ↓

    Primary references [1]

  2. Level 2 PDF 7 pages

    Noise and the Need for Fault Tolerance

    Density operators, channels and thresholds

    Density operators and quantum channels describe how correlations with the environment weaken coherence. No-cloning, continuous errors and a simple concatenation model explain how added protection can reduce logical failure under specified noise assumptions.

    Annotate →PDF ↗Download ↓

    Primary references [1]

  3. Level 3 PDF 7 pages

    Core Principles of Quantum Error Correction

    Encoding, syndromes and decoding

    Repetition, Shor and Steane codes show how to reveal error syndromes while preserving logical information. Stabilizers and correction conditions lead to parity circuits, flags and decoding, with separate attention to code distance, circuit safety and classical processing.

    Annotate →PDF ↗Download ↓

    Primary references [2]

  4. Level 4 PDF 6 pages

    Logical Operations and Magic States

    Transversal gates, lattice surgery and resource costs

    Transversal gates and joint logical measurements perform operations within an encoded space. The Eastin–Knill restriction motivates magic-state injection and distillation, linking failure budgets to physical qubits, factory throughput and computation time.

    Annotate →PDF ↗Download ↓

    Primary references [3] [4]

  5. Level 5 PDF 6 pages

    Topological Quantum Codes and 2D Color Codes

    Local checks, transversal Clifford gates, circuits and decoders

    Surface-code error chains are compared with the three-color face checks of color codes. A seven-qubit example exposes the phase conditions of transversal gates, while check weight and correlations across colors and time connect circuit design to decoding costs.

    Annotate →PDF ↗Download ↓

    Primary references [5] [6]

  6. Level 6 PDF 7 pages

    Measurement-Based Quantum Computing

    Graph states, adaptive measurements and Pauli frames

    One-bit teleportation is derived branch by branch and extended to graph states and Pauli frames. Adaptive measurement angles align random outcomes with the same logical operation, providing a route from circuits to measurement patterns.

    Annotate →PDF ↗Download ↓

    Primary references [7] [8]

  7. Level 7 PDF 7 pages

    Photonic Platforms and Topological MBQC

    Fusion, loss, RHG and FBQC

    Photon interference and Bell fusion distinguish successful outcomes, heralded failures and loss. RHG cell parities connect these records to error inference; fusion-based computing and a 2026 quantum-dot blueprint then bring optical depth, feedforward and resource supply into one design problem.

    Annotate →PDF ↗Download ↓

Preparation and review

Hyun-Jung Kim is the responsible editor, with AI assistance from OpenAI Codex. For this archival edition, AEDAUT’s ftqc_science reviewed the science and ran separate calculations; ftqc_pdf reviewed public PDF preservation, links and layout; pqc_archive_structure prepared the bilingual course guide and document connections; root integrated publication. The exact model identifier was not retained.

A separately written Python standard-library check set passed 32 named items covering 808 finite inputs, branches and binary patterns. It used at most four-qubit state vectors and matrices of dimension 16, short 7-/15-position binary patterns and scalar arithmetic to check teleportation, channels, syndromes, measurement-based CNOT, magic-state injection, color-code phase signs, adaptive MBQC branches, Bell fusion, truncated RUS and RHG cell boundaries. The original author’s reported 94-check set was reviewed as an existing record and was not rerun. No full decoder or threshold simulation, SDK/QPU run or physical optical experiment was performed. A separate human manuscript review was not established.

Editorial standards: ATRL Editorial Method 2026.08, Scientific Explanation and Visual Communication Direction 1.0, and APS reference style.
